The palettes and base maps of a map

Source: R/palettes.R
rr_palettes.Rd

rr_palettes(): eighteen palettes, each marked by use for the grid's colours, a depth's or both.

Usage

rr_palettes()

rr_basemaps()

Value

A list, each element with id and label: a palette with source, colors and use ("grid", "depth" or both); a base map with style (a MapLibre style's address) or tiles (a raster address) with maxzoom and attribution, and optionally paint (MapLibre's raster paint, such as raster-brightness-max), background (the colour beyond the picture's tiles), labels (a MapLibre style whose names are drawn over the picture, with its fonts) and label_layers (a regular expression for which of its layers: by default its symbol layers whose id starts place_, watername_ or waterway_label), or neither (none). A palette of your own, given to rr_map()'s palettes, needs id, label and colors; with no use it is offered to the grid.

Details

  • For the grid, twelve of nine colours, light (low) to dark (high). The first ten change in lightness steadily (OKLab), from viridisLite (magma, viridis, plasma) and tidyterra (deep, scotland, population_dens, etopo1_bathy, colombia_bathy, gn_yl, blues); the last two, terrain palettes, rise and fall in lightness.

  • For a depth, seven looks, the colours a dem layer offers by default (its colour$palettes), shallow to deep: quiet, pale cyan-grey to mid grey-blue, low in chroma and stopping at mid lightness, so the relief's shading reads through it (the default); seabed, sand shading into mud seen through the water, a look and not a substrate; deep, the grid's too; chart, the nautical chart's convention, the shallows blue and the deeps near white; grey, a ground for other layers, pulling no overlay's hue; and two daring ones, drained, the seabed as if the sea were drained (GMT's globe hypsometry, the deeps green lowland, the banks brown hills), and haxby, marine geology's multibeam palette, orange shallows through green to deep blue. Each ends at least 0.03 in OKLab from the light base maps' land, so the shallowest water does not read as land. They were made for a bathymetry map of Icelandic waters (2026-11-09): quiet, seabed, chart and grey designed in OKLCh, drained and haxby resampled from tidyterra to 17 stops at even steps in OKLab, their whitest stops dropped.

rr_basemaps(): base maps that show the sea floor, and none: EMODnet's sea floor (its 2020 base layer, the first and the one a map opens on), the same darkened, EMODnet's lighter atlas (v12), and Esri's ocean, which reaches beyond Europe's seas. Each is a picture with the place and sea names of a Carto style over it, Positron's on the light ones and Dark Matter's on the dark. A base map that shows a flat sea is left out: the depth is the subject.

Examples

vapply(rr_palettes(), `[[`, "", "id")
#>  [1] "magma"           "viridis"         "plasma"          "deep"           
#>  [5] "scotland"        "population_dens" "etopo1_bathy"    "colombia_bathy" 
#>  [9] "gn_yl"           "blues"           "high_relief"     "bcyr"           
#> [13] "quiet"           "seabed"          "chart"           "grey"           
#> [17] "drained"         "haxby"          
vapply(rr_basemaps(), `[[`, "", "id")
#> [1] "emodnet"       "emodnet_dark"  "emodnet_light" "ocean"        
#> [5] "none"
